title: swift: two overloads each become a wrapper around their own new overload: no extract built from the other one's evidence
kotlin: two lookalike helpers both deleted, the caller holds one of them: the inline names that one
kotlin: statements that differ only in their message string are different code: the extract does not take the other branch
ruby: a value that differs only in its symbol (fetch :error vs fetch :no_session) is not where the helper went
old:
class OpenID
  def call(env)
    return no_session unless session = env['rack.session']
    finish(session)
  end

  def no_session
    @options.
      fetch :no_session, [500, {'Content-Type'=>'text/plain'}, 'No session available.']
  end
end
new:
class OpenID
  def call(env)
    raise NoSession unless session = env['rack.session']
    finish(session)
  rescue NoSession
    @options.
      fetch :no_session, [500, {'Content-Type'=>'text/plain'}, $!.message]
  rescue
    @options.
      fetch :error, [500, {'Content-Type'=>'text/plain'}, 'OpenID has encountered an error.']
  end
end

title: kotlin: a file the parser cannot read (a class header split before an annotated constructor) gets no inline or extract
typescript: a helper inlined into two callers is still two inlines (evidence in each caller is its own)
kotlin: a plain extract next to an untouched lookalike function is still an extract
